text:
1. Johnson wrote in 1765 that Shakespeare has no heroes and that his scenes are occupied only by men.
2. Johnson's sentence about Shakespeare having no heroes has been often quoted.
3. Johnson's sentence about Shakespeare having no heroes has seldom been carefully considered.
4. Johnson intended his remark that Shakespeare has no heroes as praise.
5. In Johnson's view, other dramatists raised their characters above ordinary human proportions.
6. In Johnson's view, other dramatists gave their characters sentiments that no one ever actually felt.
7. In Johnson's view, other dramatists gave their characters language that no one ever actually used.
8. In Johnson's view, other dramatists sacrificed the reader's belief in order to gain the reader's astonishment.
9. Shakespeare's characters speak as the reader would have spoken in their situation.
10. The words of Shakespeare's characters arise from the circumstances in which they speak.
11. The circumstances in which Shakespeare's characters speak are ones the reader can imagine himself in.
